context_candidates.text: These patterns connect the report’s monitoring to the concerns of middle-income economies. More work and better-paying work help people escape poverty (refer to chapter 4). Stable, well-paid jobs also protect against falling back into poverty, and they therefore help households climb from vulnerability to security, an agenda that has particular force in locations where the vulnerable group is largest. Vulnerability to climate-related hazards—a distinct concept, reflecting the lack of the means to cope if a hazard strikes rather than the risk of falling back into poverty—extends well above the poverty line (refer to chapter 3). Vulnerability in this case means that middle-class households are also exposed to risk if social protection and financial services are lacking. The $8.30 line and the $28.00 prosperity standard are precisely the boundaries within which the middle class is found.
